chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hanan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger' up to the end of the verse
He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is not given allegiance, nor sheltered, nor given charity.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three specific legal rulings derived from the verse 'The recompense of those who wage war against Allah'?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the practical legal implications of Quran 5:33 by deriving three specific prohibitions for the *muharib* (warrior): denial of allegiance (*bay'ah*), exclusion from shelter (*i'tisam*), and ineligibility for charity (*sadaqah*). This interpretation highlights the comprehensive social and economic isolation intended as a consequence for those who wage war against the divine authority, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the tangible social markers of excommunication or penalty.
